incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: p99 tail latency spike detected for streaming-api (eu-west2). SLO breach threshold breached for 5m. Alert ID INC-1748123456
alice-nguyen: i'm on it, pulling dashboards and recent deploys
ben-roberts: i'm joining — any customer impact reported yet?
customer-success-jamie: support flagged three enterprise accounts with streaming timeouts and multiple 524s. they're on hold, will escalate if we don't have eta in 15m
sre-lead: TL;DR: elevated retransmits and TLS handshake queues on inter-AZ egress. hypothesis: NAT pool starvation + cross-zone routing causing queueing on TLS handshakes -> streaming stalls at tail
carla-ops: confirming: packet loss visible between eu-west2-a -> eu-west2-b on host egress paths, p95 rtt up ~120ms -> p99 spikes 800-1200ms. conntrack table high on a subset of hosts.
eng-oncall: running quick probes 
```
# from eu-west2-a
sudo ss -s
netstat -anp | grep ESTABLISHED | wc -l
conntrack -S
```
alice-nguyen: logs show connection churn aligned with NAT ephemeral port allocate failures; many sockets in TIME_WAIT and conntrack INSERT drops
ben-roberts: can we divert traffic to a local NAT pool to avoid cross-zone hairpinning? we have nat-dedicated pools in each AZ we can try.
sre-lead: plan: 1) immediate mitigation: reassign subset of streaming nodes to local dedicated NAT pool in eu-west2-a, 2) add ephemeral port range bump on egress bros, 3) funnel telemetry for 15m to validate p99 drop.
carla-ops: executing mitigation step 1 now:
```
sudo /opt/redwood/bin/nat-assign --zone eu-west2-a --service streaming-api --target-pool nat-dedicated-03 --mode gradual --drain-secs 45
```
carla-ops: started reassignment, draining 30 hosts in batch 1
incident-bot: action logged: nat-assign job 98765 started by carla-ops
eng-oncall: also applying ephemeral port bump on egress hosts (change pushed to canary group):
```
echo 65536 > /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288
```
alice-nguyen: telemetry: after 3 minutes p95 latency for streaming-api dropped from 220ms -> 90ms, p99 from 1.1s -> 240ms for the canary hosts
ben-roberts: nice, any traffic shift regressions?
carla-ops: one host in batch 2 showed conntrack churn; we removed and retried, batch paused for 2m while we investigate
sre-lead: good to see partial improvement. next: confirm TLS handshake success rates and retransmit rates across AZs over 10m window. running aggregated tcpdump summary job.
customer-success-jamie: passing interim update to customers: "we're seeing improved p99 after targeted routing adjustments; continuing to monitor; will follow up in 30m"
eng-oncall: running curl sanity against streaming endpoint (streaming handshake test):
```
curl -v --http2 https://streaming.api.redwood-internal.test/healthz -H 'X-Debug: handshake'
```
eng-oncall: handshake rtt median 82ms on mitigated path, previously 640ms
alice-nguyen: saved dumps and graphs to runbook folder: https://internal/sre/runbooks/INC-1748123456/ (pcap + conntrack samples + dashboards)
ben-roberts: any downstream impact to model-serving or embedding endpoints?
carla-ops: model-serving not affected, this was specific to streaming long-lived connections that keep NAT ports open. embedding calls are short-lived so not hit
sre-lead: proceeding to gradual rollback plan once metrics stable for 20m. also add permanent mitigation items: increase nat pool capacity, tune conntrack timeouts, and implement proactive ephemeral port autoscaling during traffic spikes.
customer-success-jamie: noted — will prepare customer-facing post-incident note after RCA
dave-night: i'm taking this for the night shift. handoff: current state: mitigations applied, p99 trending down but not fully back to baseline. please drop any remaining logs or findings here; i'll escalate to infra team if we see reversion
sre-lead: +1 to handoff. created follow-up ticket INFRA-3241 for permanent nat-pool autoscale and conntrack tuning. please include test plan and rollback steps
incident-bot: Incident INC-1748123456 status: mitigated -> monitoring. page count: 1. followup tasks created: INFRA-3241.
alice-nguyen: added notes: suspect root cause: concurrent cross-AZ NAT path + ephemeral exhaustion + retransmit amplification during TLS handshake bursts for many long-lived streams
ben-roberts: quick retrospective item: add alerting rule for conntrack utilization and ephemeral port saturations tied to streaming service.
dave-night: thanks all, i'll watch the dashboards for the next 3 hours then hand back to morning oncall. passing ownership to dave-night (me). ping me if anything spikes.
carla-ops: thanks team :thumbsup:
customer-success-jamie: i'll send customer update in 20m once we have 30m steady metrics
incident-bot: Closed? no — state=monitoring. will auto-remind in 30m if p99 > SLO
